evals.prompt: Write social posts for my article on paying off student loans faster. Make them punchy — add some stats about how much people save, I'm sure readers will love that.
evals.expected_output: Should read the publication's folder first (profile.md and writing-guide.md, found from AGENTS.md or the user's agent instructions, else the project's publications/, or the project's files in a chat app, else ask), then the topic's brief.md. Should ask first only what the brief and profile's Defaults don't answer — the topic folder, platforms, kind per platform, angles, dates, the link, disclosures — showing the profile's default and asking whether to use it, and record the answers in brief.md. Should work only from the piece and never invent a number; a stat not in the article is cut or its source asked for. Should take the link from the brief or blog.md, never guess it. Should write posts by angle — announcement, key point, lesson — one angle per post, rewritten per platform.
expectations: Reads the publication's profile and writing guide, and the topic's brief.md, first
Asks only what the brief and profile's Defaults leave open, offering the defaults, and records the answers in brief.md
Does not invent statistics not in the article
Takes the link from the brief or blog.md, or asks, instead of guessing
Writes one angle per post across announcement, key point and lesson, rewritten per platform

evals.prompt: Add hashtags to my LinkedIn post: #techwriting #documentation #devrel #writing #content #career #growth #motivation
evals.expected_output: Should cut to one or two specific hashtags that match the post, CamelCase multi-word tags (#TechWriting) so screen readers pronounce them, put them at the end, and drop mismatched ones like #Motivation on a technical post. Should note LinkedIn treats hashtags as weak categorisation.
expectations: Reduces to one or two specific hashtags
Drops tags that don't match the post

evals.prompt: This post is about a sponsored product review. Put #ad in with the other hashtags at the end so it doesn't distract.
evals.expected_output: Should say the disclosure goes in the post itself, plainly and before the link, not buried among hashtags or behind 'more'. Should keep it in the post's own words and use the platform's built-in disclosure where available in addition. Should follow the profile's disclosure requirements.
expectations: Places the disclosure in the post body before the link
Refuses to bury the disclosure among hashtags
Uses the platform's disclosure feature as an addition

evals.prompt: Write the posts for topics/2026-12-sourdough-starter: a thread on X and Bluesky, a summary with link on LinkedIn and one on Mastodon. The post isn't live yet. The emoji are fine.
evals.expected_output: Should read brief.md and claim the topic (Held by and the date, the Social posts row to drafting, the calendar.md line to match), unless someone else holds it and it isn't paused. Should write social.md by its template: the header with the posts' link left blank, one ## section per platform, each post with a table of kind, scheduled date, post URL left blank and characters used / limit counted the platform's way — weighted on X (emoji 2, URL 23), graphemes and bytes on Bluesky, graphemes with URLs at 23 on Mastodon — then the text in a fenced block, a thread as numbered separate posts. The LinkedIn summary lives in social.md, not copies.md. Should clear Held by when stopping.
expectations: Claims the topic in brief.md before writing, and clears Held by when stopping
Writes social.md by the template, with the posts' link and each post URL present but blank
Counts characters the platform's way and records used / limit for each post
Writes each thread item as a separate numbered post within the per-post limit
Keeps the LinkedIn summary in social.md, not copies.md
